defs.def: (used to emphasize sth) completely; in every way （用以强调）完全，全部

ex.s: Removing gender from the picture altogether seems like a simple way to fix this.
ex.t: 把性别完全从画面中剔除，似乎是解决这个问题的简单办法。

ex.s: That might mean either developing a uniform way to mark videos and images, showing when and who they were made by. or abandoning phone calls altogether and moving towards data-based communications—using apps like Face Time or WhatsApp, which can be tied to your identity.
ex.t: 这可能意味着要么开发一种统一的方式来标记视频和图像，显示它们何时以及由谁制作，要么完全放弃电话，转向使用基于数据的通信应用程序，如Face Time或WhatsApp ，这些应用程序可以与您的身份相关联。

ex.s: I forgot what he had said to me altogether.
ex.t: 我把他对我说的话全忘了。

ex.s: It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this.
ex.t: 我们这样做是完全适当的。

ex.s: In other words, if you want to be healthy, you have to cut down on desserts, and cut out sweet drinks altogether.
ex.t: 换句话说，如果你想健康，你必须减少甜点，完全切断甜饮料。

ex.s: One challenge is that the environment in space is altogether different from that back on the Earth.
ex.t: 一个挑战是太空中的环境与地球上的环境完全不同。

ex.s: How many hours of class will you have altogether if you register for a single week?
ex.t: 如果你注册一周，总共会有多少小时的课程？

ex.s: Altogether, 2,292 young people from 80 countries joined in to sing Whitacre’s song “What If”.
ex.t: 共有来自80个国家的2,292名年轻人参加了演唱Whitacre的歌曲“What If”。

ex.s: Altogether, the results of studies show that EQ is as important, if not more life requires getting on well with other people and being able to understand and react to situations in the best way possible.
ex.t: 总而言之，研究结果表明，情商同样重要，如果不是更多的生活需要与他人相处融洽，并能够以最佳方式理解和应对情况。
